name: Waveshare 7.3" e-Paper (F) on an ESP32-S3
description: Waveshare's 7.3 inch 7-colour ACeP panel (800x480, AC073TC1A) wired to an ESP32-S3 with octal PSRAM. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a 4-bpp palette-index frame (192000 bytes) in the panel's own colour order, so the firmware sends it to the controller unchanged.
notes_md:
**UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** Firmware support is the `waveshare-epaper-73f` build in tesserae-device-firmware; flash `waveshare-epaper-73f-selftest` first and check the seven colour bands (black, white, yellow, red, blue, green, orange, top to bottom).

Wire format is exactly 192000 bytes (800*480/2), row-major from the top-left, high nibble = left pixel. Nibbles follow the ACeP controller's order (0 black, 1 white, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 yellow, 6 orange), the same packing as the Inkplate 6COLOR and the original Inky Frame 7.3". This is the older 7-colour glass; Waveshare's newer 7.3 inch (E) panel is Spectra 6 and is a different kind (the PhotoPainter uses it).

**Pins.** There is no single board for this panel, so the build carries a default pin map for an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 (SCLK 12, MOSI 11, CS 10, DC 9, RST 8, BUSY 7) and each pin can be overridden at build time. The build targets a 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM module (N16R8).

No battery reporting and no buttons.
